observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: Three independent callsites were disassembled and all three show PUSH <ptr>; CALL 0x005a9200; ADD ESP,0x4, i.e. the caller pops the argument. 0x0064b416/0x0064b417/0x0064b41c, 0x00e84668/0x00e8467b/0x00e84685 and the call at 0x005a95ea inside 0x005a94d0. The function's own epilogue is POP EDI; POP ESI; MOV AL,0x1; POP EBX; RET at 0x005a9460..0x005a9465 with a bare RET and no immediate, and the three pushes at 0x005a9200..0x005a9202 are matched by the three pops, so no callee-side stack argument is popped.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: unconditional true; the only write to the return register is MOV AL,0x1 at 0x005a9462, so bits 8..31 of EAX are undefined on exit. All three inspected callers discard the value.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x005a9462: MOV AL,0x1 writes only the low byte. The body contains no other write to EAX after the last callee return, so nothing else is defined in the return register.
observed_original_abi.termination: single exit at 0x005a9465; no early return exists in the 199-instruction body
observed_original_abi.saved_registers_observation: PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI at 0x005a9200..0x005a9202, POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX at 0x005a9460..0x005a9464. Balanced, so the frame is a plain three-register save with no locals spilled to the stack; max observed ESP displacement inside the body is [ESP+0x10] at 0x005a9211.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX is never read before the first call and is only ever loaded as an explicit argument (0x005a92be, 0x005a92e1, 0x005a9276, 0x005a945c) or used as scratch (0x005a92a6 XOR ECX,ECX, 0x005a92f9 XOR ECX,ECX, 0x005a9450 MOV ECX,EAX, 0x005a92ef MOV ECX,EAX). There is no callee-side this.
observed_original_abi.frame: no SUB ESP and no MOV EBP,ESP: the argument is read at [ESP+0x10] because three registers are already pushed

observed_mechanics: 0x005a9200..0x005a9202: PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI opens the frame
0x005a9203: CALL 0x0067dd10, the two-instruction getter returning [0x015fd8b0]; Ghidra carries the SDK symbol Graphics::IRenderer::Get
0x005a9208/0x005a920c/0x005a920f: MOV EDX,[EAX]; MOV EAX,[EDX+0x38]; CALL EAX with ECX still the renderer, i.e. virtual slot +0x38 of Graphics::IRenderer, no stack argument
0x005a9211: MOV EDI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] is the sole argument, read after three pushes so it is the entry [ESP+4]
0x005a9215: LEA EDX,[EDI + 0x24] takes the address of the 4 x int32 block
0x005a9218: MOV dword ptr [EDI + 0x1c],EAX stores the renderer slot +0x38 result into the argument's field at +0x1c

0x005a9220..0x005a922c: the four-iteration zero test, CMP dword ptr [ECX],0x0 / INC EAX / ADD ECX,0x4 / CMP EAX,0x4 / JC, so exactly four dwords at +0x24,+0x28,+0x2c,+0x30 are examined and a non-zero one leaves EAX non-zero
0x005a9223: JNZ 0x005a924f is the early exit that skips the seeding block
0x005a922e: MOV ECX,dword ptr [0x015da7c4] loads the first of four consecutive globals
0x005a9234/0x005a923b/0x005a9244/0x005a924c: the four stores copy 0x015da7c4, 0x015da7c8, 0x015da7cc and 0x015da7d0 into +0x24, +0x28, +0x2c and +0x30

0x015da7c4 is an all-zero image in the file (ghidra_read_memory returns 24 zero bytes), so the seed data is built at runtime; the Ghidra SDK symbol at that address is Editors::ContentValidation::sIllegalCharacters
0x005a924f: CMP dword ptr [EDI + 0xc],0xffffffff tests the -1 sentinel
0x005a9253: JNZ 0x005a9260 skips the resolver when the field is already set, so the resolver runs at most once per call
0x005a9255: LEA EAX,[EDI + 0x10] passes the address of the field at +0x10 to the resolver in EAX, a register argument rather than a thiscall
0x005a925d: MOV dword ptr [EDI + 0xc],EAX writes the resolved id back into +0x0c
0x005a9260: CALL 0x0067dcc0, the getter returning [0x015fd890]; Ghidra carries the SDK symbol App::IAppSystem::Get
0x005a9267: MOV ESI,EAX caches the singleton pointer in ESI for both later calls
0x005a9269/0x005a926b: MOV EDX,[ESI]; MOV EAX,[EDX + 0x18] reads virtual slot +0x18
0x005a9265/0x005a926e/0x005a9270/0x005a9271: four pushes, giving the stack arguments 0xb03bc30c, EDI, 0, 0 in that order
0x005a9276/0x005a9278: MOV ECX,ESI; CALL EAX, so the singleton is the receiver and four stack arguments are passed
0x005a927a..0x005a9287: six pushes giving 0x40, 0x013ebc58, 0, 0, 0, 0 as the arguments, in that order
0x013ebc58 holds the NUL-terminated ASCII string "App" followed by 0x41 ('A') padding; ghidra_read_memory at 0x013ebc58 returns 41 70 70 00
0x005a928e: ADD ESP,0x18 proves the six arguments are caller-cleanup
0x005a9291/0x005a9293: TEST EAX,EAX; JZ 0x005a9356 is the only null check on the allocation

0x005a9356/0x005a9358: the allocation-failure path sets EBX to 0 and jumps to 0x005a92c5, which is MOV dword ptr [EBX + 0x30],0xe11332 at 0x005a92c7, i.e. a write to linear address 0x30. The original does not survive a failed allocation; the fault is preserved rather than repaired.
0x005a9299: MOV dword ptr [EAX + 0x30],0x0 clears the field that will hold the message id
0x005a92a0: MOV dword ptr [EAX],0x13eb90c installs the derived vtable
0x005a92a6/0x005a92a8/0x005a92ab: XOR ECX,ECX; LEA EDX,[EAX + 0x4]; XCHG dword ptr [EDX],ECX zeroes field +4 and moves the previous field +4 into ECX
0x005a92ad: MOV dword ptr [EAX],0x13eb844 replaces the derived vtable with the base vtable before the base slots are used, the standard two-level construction order
0x005a92b3: MOV dword ptr [EAX + 0x38],0x0
0x005a92bc/0x005a92be/0x005a92c0: MOV EBX,EAX; MOV ECX,EAX; MOV EAX,[EDX + 0x4] reads vtable slot +4 of 0x013eb844
0x013eb844 read live: +0x00 = 0x004230e0, +0x04 = 0x00432a50, +0x08 = 0x00404f90, then the literals "queuing %ls for bake\n" at +0x0c and "No key -- you need to save the model first.\n" at +0x22
0x00432a50 body: LOCK; INC [this+4]; return old value, an AddRef on a refcount at +4
0x005a92c7: MOV dword ptr [EBX + 0x30],0xe11332 writes the message id

0x005a92d0: MOV dword ptr [EBX + 0x8],0xdbdba1. 0x00dbdba1 lies in .text and ghidra_read_memory there returns instruction bytes (11 44 24 14 f3 0f ...), so 0x00dbdba1 is an odd id immediate, not a pointer
0x005a92c5/0x005a92ce/0x005a92df/0x005a92e0: four pushes giving 0x00e11332, EBX, 0, 0
0x005a92d7/0x005a92dc/0x005a92e1/0x005a92e3: the second call through virtual slot +0x18 of the same singleton, with the message object as the payload
0x005a92ea: CALL 0x0067cab0. ghidra_disassemble_function at 0x0067cab0 returns exactly two instructions, MOV EAX,[0x015fcc50]; RET, so the 0x1003 push is NOT consumed by this call
0x005a92ef: MOV ECX,EAX makes the global's value the receiver

0x005a92f1: CALL 0x00801bb0 therefore consumes the 0x1003 as its single stack argument. Its decompiled body is a map find keyed by 0x1003 that may call 0x008027e0, and the returned bool is never read by the target, so this is a side-effecting cache probe whose answer is discarded.
0x005a92f6: MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDI + 0xc] loads the switch key, the same field the resolver may have written
0x005a92f9: XOR ECX,ECX establishes bit index 0, the no-match value, which is why no arm can produce 0..4

0x005a92fb..0x005a94bc: 34 distinct comparison constants in a hand-rolled JG/JZ binary search, no indexed load and therefore no jump table. Every arm ends in MOV ECX,<5|6|7|8|9|a|b|c|d|e|f>; JMP 0x005a9427
0x005a9306/0x005a930b: CMP EAX,0x1d2ec0a4 / JGE 0x005a93d4 together with CMP EAX,0x1d2ec0a7 / JG at 0x005a92fb..0x005a9300 make 0x1d2ec0a4..0x1d2ec0a7 one four-value range, not four cases
0x005a9422/0x005a9466/0x005a948d/0x005a94ad/0x005a94b7 are the shared arm heads for bits 6, 0xb, 0xc, 0xa and 9, each reached by several JZ
0x005a9427: MOV EAX,[0x015fd918] is the first of the two dependent property loads
0x005a942c: MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x3c] is the second
0x005a942f/0x005a9436: CMP dword ptr [EDX + 0x118],0x0 / JNZ 0x005a9457, so a non-zero property skips the entire mask block
0x005a9438/0x005a943a: TEST ECX,ECX / JZ 0x005a9457, the second guard, so an unmatched id also skips it
0x005a943c/0x005a9441: MOV EAX,0x1; SHL EAX,CL builds the single-bit mask 1 << bit
0x005a9443/0x005a9445/0x005a9446: three pushes giving 0x00d082675a, mask, 1
0x005a944b: CALL 0x00675250. ghidra_disassemble_function shows it is a bare getter of [0x015fc250] with a RET that has no immediate, so it consumes none of the three pushed words
0x005a9450: MOV ECX,EAX makes the global the receiver of the next call

0x005a9452: CALL 0x00676ed0 therefore receives the three words as its stack arguments. ghidra_disassemble_function at 0x00676ed0 shows PUSH ESI / PUSH ESI-relative body / POP ESI / RET 0xC, so exactly three stack arguments are popped

0x00676ed0 body: CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x24],0 / JNZ exit, then record = FUN_00676660(arg2), then OR [EAX+4],arg2 when arg3 != 0 else AND [EAX+4],~arg2, then if ([EAX] & 1) and FUN_006751c0(EAX) then FUN_00676710(arg2). arg1, the value 0x00d082675a at [ESP+0] on entry, is never read: the only stack-slot reads are [ESP+0xc] and [ESP+0x10] with ESP already lowered by two pushes, i.e. the original's second argument, and [ESP+0x14], i.e. the third.
0x005a9457/0x005a9459/0x005a945c/0x005a945e: MOV EDX,[EBX]; MOV EAX,[EDX + 0x8]; MOV ECX,EBX; CALL EAX, virtual slot +8 of the message object
0x00404f90 body: LOCK; DEC [this+4]; on reaching zero set [this+1] = 1 and call (*(this->vtable))[0] with argument 1, a Release
0x005a9462: MOV AL,0x1 is the only write to the return register
0x005a9465: RET is bare, so the callee pops no stack words

control_flow.shape: single basic block chain with one 4-iteration counted loop and one comparison ladder; no switch table, no computed jump
control_flow.loop: 0x005a9220..0x005a922c, four iterations over the dwords at +0x24..+0x30, exiting early via JNZ 0x005a924f on the first non-zero dword; the JC at 0x005a922c runs the body exactly four times when all are zero
early_exits: 0x005a9223 JNZ 0x005a924f - a non-zero mEditableTests dword skips the seed
0x005a9253 JNZ 0x005a9260 - a non -1 mEditorName skips the resolver
0x005a9293 JZ 0x005a9356 - a failed allocation falls into a guaranteed fault (see observed_mechanics)
0x005a9436 JNZ 0x005a9457 - a non-zero App property at +0x118 skips the mask write
0x005a943a JZ 0x005a9457 - bit index 0 skips the mask write
every ladder arm that matches jumps to 0x005a9427, the single merge point
branch_polarity: 0x005a9220 CMP [ECX],0x0 / 0x005a9223 JNZ: non-zero means 'already set, do not seed'
0x005a9291 TEST EAX,EAX / 0x005a9293 JZ: null allocation takes the faulting path
0x005a942f CMP [EDX+0x118],0 / 0x005a9436 JNZ: non-zero property means 'do not touch the flags'
0x005a9438 TEST ECX,ECX / 0x005a943a JZ: zero bit index means 'unmapped id, do not touch the flags'
0x00676ed0 0x00676ee4 CMP byte [ESP+0x14],0 / 0x00676ee9 JZ: the polarity argument, non-zero selects OR (set), zero selects AND-NOT (clear)
control_flow.ladder_result_range: 5..15 inclusive, or 0 for an unmatched id. Values 1,2,3,4 are unreachable: the only zeroing instruction is XOR ECX,ECX and no arm writes those values.

semantic_contract: Editors::EditorRequest::Submit(Editors::EditorRequest* request) always reports success (it returns the byte 1) and its whole effect is a side effect on three things. First, it stamps the request's calling-game-mode field: it asks Graphics::IRenderer for its slot +0x38 value and writes the result to request+0x1c, overwriting whatever the caller had put there. Second, it guarantees the request carries an editable-content policy: if all four dwords of request+0x24 are zero it seeds them from the runtime-built Editors::ContentValidation::sIllegalCharacters object at 0x015da7c4, and if request+0x0c is still the -1 'editor not chosen' sentinel it resolves the editor id from the request's model ResourceKey and writes it back. Third, it announces the request and then records progress: it emits two notifications through one singleton interface's slot +0x18, first with id 0xb03bc30c carrying the request, then with id 0x00e11332 carrying a freshly allocated 0x40-byte App object whose own fields are 0x00e11332 at +0x30 and the id constant 0x00dbdba1 at +0x08, and it AddRefs that object at construction and Releases it before returning. Alongside that it probes the singleton at 0x015fcc50 with the constant 0x1003 and throws the answer away, so only that probe's side effect can matter. Finally, if the App property at [[0x015fd918]+0x3c]+0x118 is zero and the resolved editor id is one of 34 known ids, it maps that id to a bit index in 5..15 and sets exactly that one bit in a 32-bit progress mask via the call at 0x00676ed0, whose first argument 0x00d082675a is pushed but never read. An unrecognised id leaves the index at 0 and touches nothing. The allocation failure path is not handled: a null return is written through, faulting at linear address 0x30.
classification_rationale: The body, ABI, every field offset, every constant, every global, the whole control-flow graph and all six dispatch sites were read directly from the disassembly and corroborated by three disassembled callers, a sibling builder at 0x005a94d0 that writes the same object, and an SDK header whose ASSERT_SIZE(0x9C), sentinel value and member offsets agree with the observed layout field for field. That rules out STRUCTURAL_ONLY and STILL_UNKNOWN. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because three material elements are bounded rather than established: (1) the interface behind the singleton at 0x015fd890 is unidentified -- it has exactly one writer, 0x0067deb0, with no callers, and the observed four-argument shape at slot +0x18 contradicts the SDK's IAppSystem::InitPlugins, so the two notifications are named only by their raw ids; (2) 0x00676ed0 is attributed to Pollinator::cAchievementsManager as a class on five SDK addresses inside its own code block, but SetProgressFlags as the specific method is a body-shape inference because the SDK's declared address for that method resolves to a neighbouring near-identical function; (3) the class of the 0x40-byte App object is established only as a three-slot IMessageRC-shaped refcounted message with two adjacent bake-related string literals -- no vtable beyond 0x013eb844/0x013eb90c was located for it, so no SDK class name is claimed for it.
semantic_findings: The function always returns true; the return is a byte and no caller inspected uses it.
It is a mutator of its argument, not a query: it overwrites request+0x1c with Graphics::IRenderer slot +0x38 and request+0x0c with a resolved editor id.
request+0x24 is Editors::ContentValidation, four int32 flags, and the 'all zero' test is a genuine all-zero test over exactly four dwords, not a null check.
The -1 sentinel on request+0x0c makes the resolver idempotent: a caller that pre-sets the id suppresses the lookup entirely.
The 34-way ladder is a hand-rolled binary search with no jump table, and 0x1d2ec0a4..0x1d2ec0a7 is a single range arm, not four cases.
Bit indices 1..4 are unreachable; the only zeroing instruction is XOR ECX,ECX, so the observed output alphabet is exactly {0} union {5..15}.

0x0067cab0 and 0x00675250 are bare two-instruction getters whose RET has no immediate, which is what lets the 0x1003 and the three mask words pass through them to the following calls. The decompiler's rendering of those calls as consuming their own arguments is wrong.
The call to 0x00676ed0 passes four values for three stack slots; its first argument is provably unread.

0x00432f10, reached only through 0x005a8f80, produces ids from the same set this function's ladder consumes and reads the same [[0x015fd918]+0x3c]+0x118 property, so the resolver and the flag write are two halves of one feature gate.

The TypeIDs read in 0x005a8f80's fallback (crt, vcl, bld, cll, ufo, flr) are the six model types in Spore/CommonIDs.h, and crt maps to 0x465c50ba, which Spore/Editors/Editor.h line 340 documents as cEditor::mEditorName. So a creature model key selects the creature editor.
The function does not survive a failed allocation: the null path writes to linear address 0x30.
0x00dbdba1 is an id constant, not a pointer: the address is inside .text and holds instruction bytes.
